#6285. 50 Travel Gifts Under $50 They'll Actually Use on Their Next Trip

Travel buffs can be surprisingly difficult to shop for. They probably already have a suitcase they love, noise-canceling headphones, and enough packing cubes to last them a lifetime. Instead of adding to their collection of travel essentials, consider something they wouldn't necessarily buy for themselves. It doesn't have to be expensive, either. The best travel gifts will upgrade every journey, whether it’s a smart gadget to help make a red-eye flight less miserable or a sweet reminder of their favorite destination—all without breaking the bank.

With this in mind, I’ve rounded up 50 thoughtful gifts under $50 to give this season, from personalized accessories to luxe skincare sets. Whether you're shopping for a frequent flier, an avid road tripper, or a friend with a growing list of places to visit, there's something here for every traveler on your list—including yourself.

Every traveler needs a sturdy duffel bag for weekend road trips. This under-$30 weekender has enough space for two to three days' worth of clothes, as well as a separate shoe compartment and pockets for small travel accessories. Plus, it fits underneath a plane seat and features a luggage sleeve.

This large makeup bag has earned over 13,000 reviews for its practical design, which opens flat so you can see everything inside without rummaging through it. It also has a few interior pockets, a separate brush compartment, and a water-resistant exterior that’s easy to wipe clean.

L.L.Bean's classic Boat and Tote bag holds everything you need for a day trip and packs completely flat in your carry-on. It's great for storing souvenirs or to have just in case.

True to its name, this bag can be used for a variety of things; it’s roomy enough to fill up with snacks, charging cords, or the jumble of in-flight necessities that usually float around in the bottom of your tote. It has a water-resistant lining and multiple interior and exterior pockets for easy access.

Bagsmart's lightweight backpack is a practical gift for travelers who are always headed on a weekend getaway or could use a new personal item for the plane. Unlike a traditional backpack, it features a clamshell opening, so you can see all of your belongings at once and pack items like you would in a suitcase. The adjustable straps can even be clasped over your chest, making it more secure and comfortable.

Ditch the bulky purse with this crossbody phone case, made from genuine Italian leather. It features an adjustable, removable strap you can wear crossbody or around your neck. The protective case helps guard against drops, and there's even a handy card slot on the back for your credit card or ID. It's available for iPhone 16 and 17 models.

Made from 100% mulberry silk, this sleep mask feels soft against your skin while blocking out light for some much-needed shut-eye. The contoured eye cups leave room to blink without pressing on your lashes, and the adjustable strap keeps it comfortably in place.

The hard outer shell of this case protects jewelry during travels, while little nooks, slot rolls, and hooks keep earrings, necklaces, and bracelets separated and tangle-free. It's small enough to pack on quick trips while being roomy enough for destination weddings and longer vacations.

A weighted eye mask is a thoughtful gift for any frequent flier. This soothing mask is ideal for side sleepers or back sleepers, and keeps you comfortable at home and on the road.

A reliable travel pillow is an essential on every long-haul flight. What really sets this Cabeau pillow apart from the rest is the Velcro straps on the back, designed to loop around a plane seat's headrest, helping to keep your head upright and take any pressure off your neck.

This small but mighty stocking stuffer is bound to get used right away, especially if your giftee is frequently on the go. Attach it to everything from keys to luggage to keep tabs on the item using the accompanying app on your iPhone.

Leakproof, magnetic, and practically indestructible, these TSA-friendly mini jars are great for decanting your toiletries, medication, or anything else that fits, for carry-on travel.

Keep charging cables, earbuds, adapters, and other small tech essentials from getting lost in your bag with this leather organizer from Mark & Graham. Its slim design and snap closure make it easy to pack for trips or daily commutes.

Choose from a variety of fonts, colors, and designs to customize this passport cover for the international traveler in your life. Pro tip: A bonus of going with a brighter color is that it’s easier to find in your bag when you need it.

This leather luggage tag from Tumi adds a little personality to your suitcase while making it easier to spot on the baggage carousel. Available in more than 20 colors and customizable with a monogram, it's a small but thoughtful gift for frequent travelers.

Available in six vibrant color combos, these handcrafted leather card cases hold up to five cards or, thanks to the snap closure, can be used to stash foreign coins that accumulate when traveling internationally.

If your friend is always reading a book on their Kindle, gift them a fun case that will protect their device from accidental drops. Casely’s Kindle cover is durable yet lightweight, so they can slip it into a weekender bag or backpack without it weighing them down.

This tiny, portable reading light packs a powerful punch. It attaches securely to your book and has a swiveling head with two brightness levels. Plus, it’s rechargeable via USB, with a battery life long enough to cover multiple page-turners’ worth of reading.

Small enough to fit in the palm of your hand or clip onto a bag, this mini keychain camera is a fun way to capture travel memories with a nostalgic twist. It takes photos and videos, has retro-inspired filters, and comes in one of seven surprise designs. Note that you'll need to buy a memory card separately.

Waterproof, dustproof, and practically everything-proof, this pocket-sized speaker is perfect for streaming your favorite tunes or podcasts while on the go. It’s available in eight fun color combos, and the best part is its durability: You can bring it on your beach vacation without worrying when it inevitably gets sandy.

Owala is known for its fun-colored water bottles, but its travel mugs are equally amazing. This 12-ounce mug keeps coffee or tea hot for hours and is completely leakproof. Plus, it's available in a slew of bright colors.

Whether serving your beverage neat or on the rocks, these insulated stainless steel tumblers are designed to last through countless happy hours in the backyard or backcountry. They also pack up neatly in a wool felt case for easy carrying.

Lounge comfortably in your own backyard with this outdoor camping hammock. It folds down into a small storage pouch, and is incredibly lightweight while still able to hold up to 400 pounds.

For any outdoorsy traveler on your list, you can't go wrong with a classic Swiss Army knife. It fits in a small fanny pack or sling bag and comes in handy for hiking or camping adventures.

A set of rechargeable hand warmers like this two-pack can keep your fingers warm for up to 12 hours on a three-hour charge, and means you don't have to abandon exploring some magnificent winter wonderland vistas due to the chill.

Compact, durable, and endlessly reliable, this straw filter is an adventurer's essential—capable of transforming even the murkiest stream into safe, drinkable water. It’s the kind of smart, ultralight gear you’ll be glad to have on hand, whether you’re trekking through the backcountry or navigating an off-the-grid escape.

Made from certified post-consumer recycled plastic, this ultra-absorbent towel can be used for yoga, camping, the pool, and pretty much everything in between. It’s also guaranteed to stand out on the beach courtesy of the vibrant print options available, from classic stripes to national park–inspired patterns.

No need to settle for bad hotel coffee. These compact, individually packaged syrups (about the size of a tea bag) are easy to travel with, so you can perfect your morning latte every time. The variety pack includes flavors like rose vanilla, lavender honey, pistachio coconut, and salted pecan praline.

A warm cardigan is an essential for chilly fall and winter mornings. Throw on this one to run errands, venture out to a museum, grab coffee (or a cocktail), and, well, pretty much anything in between.

Another one of our favorite staples from Quince is this cashmere crewneck. It's super-soft, lightweight, and works for just about any winter getaway.

With over 10,000 Amazon reviews, these best-selling slippers are made for cozy days at home. They have a soft, fuzzy lining, cloud-like memory foam cushioning, and nonslip soles for the occasional trip outside. Even better, they're machine washable.

This sock-meet-slipper bootie has a soft brushed lining and grippy bottoms and comes in everything from heathered neutrals to festive Fair Isle patterns.

Cold hands are no match for these Quince gloves, made from 100% Mongolian cashmere. The longer cuffs provide extra coverage on chilly days, while touchscreen-friendly fingertips mean you won't have to take them off every time you reach for your phone.

Whether you're having a bad hair day or are just going for that model-off-duty look, Todd Snyder's Dad cap elevates any airport uniform. It's made from the same Japanese selvedge used in the brand's best-selling Chinos.

These Bombas socks add a little luxury to an everyday essential with a soft, cozy blend of merino wool and cashmere. They're thick and warm without sacrificing breathability, with built-in arch support and a seamless toe for added comfort. They come in three sizes—small, medium, and large—for a more personalized fit.

Socks might not seem like the most exciting gift to open on Christmas morning, but Todd Snyder's Argyle dress socks will have you thinking differently. Made in Italy with a cotton blend, they're soft and sophisticated enough for the most special of occasions.

Land at your destination feeling refreshed by popping on Rhode's depuffing eye patches. These hydrating patches actually stay in place without sliding around.

Give dry, tired skin a little TLC with the Summer Fridays Jet Lag Essentials Set, featuring four travel-size bestsellers: a hydrating face mist, serum, moisturizing mask, and depuffing eye patches.

This limited-edition Rhode set pairs the brand's creamy Pocket Blush with its glossy Peptide Lip Tint for an easy pop of color on the go. Both formulas are hydrating and buildable, and the set comes in three coordinated shade combinations, from soft pink to warm brown to mauve.

Keep dry hands soft and moisturized on the go with this L'Occitane gift set. It includes three travel-sized hand creams made in France, featuring the brand's signature shea butter, warm almond, and calming lavender scents. They're just the right size to tuck into a purse, carry-on, or desk drawer.

Whether you’re looking for relief after a marathon of luggage-laden travel or a little help unwinding from back-to-back Zoom meetings, this soothing botanical blend of lavender, ginger root, and geranium provides just the right dose of self-care in a TSA-approved rollerball size. Pro tip: Dab it on your pulse points and pair with an eye mask and noise-canceling headphones for brief moments of zen.

There’s nothing more relaxing than a soothing scalp massage. This beautiful, weighty comb is carved from jade (and comes in varying shades of serene green). It is designed to relieve tension and help stimulate circulation. It’s perfect for pairing with your favorite hair treatment for a calming self-care ritual.

Infused with aloe and botanical extracts, this skin-softening cleanser from New York City–based Le Labo can be used head-to-toe—taking a simple act of hygiene to the next level with its classic yet luxurious scent of lavender, bergamot, and violet.

Formulated with five ultra-nourishing oils and butters (cocoa, sweet almond, apricot kernel, fractionated coconut, and avocado), this sculptural moisturizer softens as it comes into contact with warm, dry skin. Bask in the calming mix of woody vetiver and zesty bergamot, and use it as a massage stone for an incredibly relaxing and indulgent self-care ritual that rivals a day at your favorite spa.

Give the gift of great skin with Merit Beauty's best-selling serum. This mini size is TSA-approved and fits nicely in any Dopp kit.

Merit's Flush cream blush is just the right size to keep in your purse for quick, on-the-go touches. It melts effortlessly into the skin and makes blending in your blush easier than ever.

Raw, sustainably sourced, and utterly therapeutic, these wildcrafted honeys are hand-harvested from apiaries around the country. Break up the set to gift as foodie stocking stuffers—or hoard one or two for yourself.

These beautiful color-blocked teaspoons from Australian brand Fazeek are hand-blown from durable borosilicate glass, and are useful for drizzling toppings or mixing concoctions. They make for a memorable gift for the foodie friend who has everything.

Bring a taste of the Italian coast home with this Voluspa candle, which blends bright scents of Sicilian lemon and bergamot with notes of jasmine and warm amber. Plus, the embossed glass jar and metal lid make it pretty enough to leave on display.

A unique gift for the Francophile in your life, these wax discs by storied candle brand Carrière Frères can be used in suitcases, closets, or the car—anywhere you’d like to add a soft lavender scent. They also double as a fragrant ornament, and thanks to the ornate packaging, require no additional wrapping.

#6284. We Keep Going Back To Germany. This Family Trip Reminded Me Why.

We landed in Zürich on SAS and drove to my in-law’s home in Southwest Germany, about an hour away.

There are border checks now as you enter Germany from France and Switzerland, though usually (I’m just saying…) when they see it’s white people they just waive you through.

And I’ll leave off the politics here (because I’d rather focus on getting our own house in order in the USA), but I think this picture says it all about Germany these days:

We tend to stop at DM (a drug store chain) at the start of each trip because it’s on the way home and we always come with a list since so many products here are cheaper and better than their American counterparts, even with the stronger Euro. One thing I like about DM (well, liked…) was that they had a free water dispenser with cups.

In Germany water is an annoyance when going out…most restaurants and coffee shops frown on tap water (unlike in France and the Netherlands), so you’re paying everywhere €5-8EUR for bottles you can buy for 50-80 Euro cents in the grocery store. It’s nice to “hydrate” at DM, but for TWO YEARS the water machine has been broken.

How in the heck can you not fix this for two years (unless, as I suppose, the point is that you don’t want to offer free water any longer)?!

It was a bit warm for the time of the year, but not unpleasant. How nice it was to be back and over the next several days we enjoyed a lot of quality time together, with good döner, coffee, and ice cream.

There was a fairly intense lighting storm that was just beautiful to sit out on the patio and watch:

One morning I decided to ride by myself to Basel for coffee…there was a new place I wanted to try called Mantila Coffee…it was SO GOOD (my new favorite coffee spot in Basel) and I had such a nice chat with the owner. I’m going to update my Basel Coffee post with a couple of places I tried on this trip.

Augustine was livid that biked to Basel without him, so we returned the next day (sadly Mantila is closed on Saturday), but we found another great place called Tinka. Augustine wanted his own coffee…I had a cortado, he had cappuccino, and then we split a delicious sparkling blood orange drink.

My father-in-law likes a restaurant called Gasthaus Krone in the hamlet of Lehnacker, located really right in the middle of the Schwarzwald (Black Forest). The food is delicious indeed.

One cool part of this trip is that my daughter finally got the hang of riding her bike herself…we just don’t feel it’s safe to ride bikes at home (due to fast drivers…see here for a laugh) but it was fun to see her so excited.

To celebrate, we had (more) ice cream together.

Matthew is an avid traveler who calls Los Angeles home. Each year he travels more than 200,000 miles by air and has visited more than 135 countries. Time in the city and time in the country. Travel and family. Time spent in community (faith based or otherwise). Coffee. All are non-optional for a well lived life. Hope you enjoyed the trip.

Enjoy Augustine being livid at being left out. Assuming he is emotionally healthy, you have only a few years before he concludes you are a square he wants to avoid.

4 Swiss Francs for an espresso that costs 1 Euro in Italy. Oh well…….

I really enjoy visiting Germany. Unfortunately my language skills are near zero.

And yeah, the politics/issues in Germany are also not good at times. I have an Italian friend who lives north of Munich and was telling us of issues. Her son is finishing up college/school there and actually has 4 different passports.

Most of our trips have been the typical shorter tourist trips but I would like a multi-week trip to explore the countryside.

Keep taking the trips, even if the kids miss a bit of school. As the child of parents that placed high value on family, travel and experiences, I learned far more visiting family in Germany and traveling Europe than I did sitting in the classroom.

Very nice. Thanks for sharing the slice of life with us.

#6283. Wander.com: Best Luxury Take On Airbnb (With Real Value Too?)

At first, the big hotel chains of the world laughed off Airbnb and vacation rentals. No seriously, they did. Now, they all compete in the vacation rental business and act like it was always the plan.

The problem for the traveler, is that almost all of the newer entrants just plug into a massive pipeline of already existing vacation homes and apartments and pop them on their own branded website with no added luxury, differentiation, amenity or expertise in curation.

There’s no huge unlock of new places or highly curated places that you could virtually always stamp as worth recommending to a friend, the way you’d rate an Aman, St. Regis, or Four Seasons hotel.

This is precisely where Wander.com comes in, and it’s by far my favorite luxe vacation rental platform to date. The fact that it’s boutique and limited is what makes it, at least for me. And, the $350 off Wander promo code doesn’t hurt either.

Wander is a vacation rental company which truly hand picks every property that it lists, and has the exclusive listing on. Crucially, each of the vacation properties undergoes a sort of ‘Wander’ transformation to conform with brand standards for wifi, amenity, style and vibe.

It’s above my pay-grade as a blogger on this topic, but it seems like Wander co-invests in the real estate portfolio’s, or partners with owners in a unique way that’s far more integrated than others.

Where are they? Most Wander.com properties are scattered across the US, from the shores of Malibu to the great National Parks in Wyoming and all along the Eastern seaboard too. Hawaii is also a recent addition. New destinations keep popping up!

Each of their properties feels uniquely wonderful and aspirational, and I’d say all have a very modern and contemporary slant to luxury. Grandma’s cabinets are not in any of these homes, but Tesla chargers are. One nice touch: each Wander offers a dedicated workspace with desk, chair, monitors and lightning fast wifi.

I completely respect that all tastes are individual, but the interiors and setups of these homes much more reflect my personal tastes, more minimalist chic, than many less curated vacation rental options.

Most Wander properties are around $1000 a night. Some will be half that, some will be double. On its face, that’s intimidating to many, but when you factor in the number of bedrooms and features it’s really reasonable. Families, or multi-family get togethers… amazing.

All Wander.com properties are at least two bedrooms and many are four, five or even twelve. One is an entire island with multiple residential complexes. For me, I love these sort of getaways for catching up with family or friends, and I never mind when other people are contributing too.

We’ve had some of our best ever vacations renting a house in Palm Springs for weeks or months at a time. Often, family or friends want in too, so we split the house and end up with two bedrooms each for under $500 per night.

We’ve used these bonus rooms and features to socialize or catch up with people in the serenity of the home, not annoyed by service, crowded pools or tight room setups. For a longer stay, I absolutely hate having to rely on a hotel kitchen for every meal. I love to hit a local market and grill with family or guests.

Wander is offering $350 off first bookings, which is a great way to get started. To browse the homes, you simply download the Wander app and start doom scrolling. When you find one you’re ready to book, the process is very self explanatory and easy to share with others.

I’m personally a fan of virtually California vacation and the properties offered on the platform cover everything from Palm Springs to Napa and all in between in stunning form. The $350 off is a solid discount and combined with new property discounts, which are frequent, there is a lot to love. You can browse Wander and download the app here.

If you don’t see the Wander.com discount in your account, you can add promo code AKFVDFD7 once the app is downloaded.

#6282. 7 Best Hotels in Antigua, the Caribbean Island With a Beach for Every Day of the Year

With endless white-sand beaches, acres of rugged rainforest, and plenty of untouched tangle just waiting to be explored, the best hotels in Antigua celebrate its landscape, which remains largely true to how nature intended. Most of the properties on this glorious Caribbean island are a stone’s throw from the crystal-clear waters that lap its powder-soft shores. It’s a beach-lover’s dream, and anyone visiting would be hard-pressed to see every stretch of golden sand—as the saying goes, there’s “a beach for every day of the year” here (yes, an even 365).

Visit between June and October, and you might just be lucky enough to watch baby turtles emerging blurry-eyed from their shells before scuttling to the sea. There are optimal times for surfing here, too, but the year-round promise is that the vibe on this island is chill. Days stretch lazily from sunrise swims to rum-fueled sundowners, with the opportunity for a poolside snooze in between. It’s easy to sink into vacation mode here, especially when you’re checking into one of the best hotels in Antigua. We've rounded up the most luxurious options on the island below, from high-end resorts with all the frills to boutique hideaways so good you’ll be booking your return before you’ve even left for home.

This intimate boutique hotel located on the south coast of the island oozes classic Caribbean charm in spades. A colonial-style whitewashed building forms the central part of the 20-acre estate, encircled by outbuildings awash in baby pink and shaded by lush, leafy palms. Thanks to the hotel’s unique perch on a secluded promontory, you’ll be flanked by azure-blue waters on all sides: Guests can lounge at the hotel’s two beaches entirely undisturbed, with only peppy team members coming around intermittently with drinks and ice pops. Days here are spent lolling by the two pools and working up a sweat at the four (yes, four!) tennis courts, before ending with relaxed Caribbean dinners and live jazz. —Sophie Knight

This resort is a true slice of paradise, and the kind of place you'll be itching to return to the moment you leave. Expect utter peace, relaxing accommodations, excellent food, and a plethora of water activities. The spacious, contemporary cottages—30 in all—feature rattan accents, white linens, and mosquito-netted beds that create a Balinese-esque look, while hideaway TVs encourage you to unplug a little (at least until it's dark outside). The decks are nearly as large as the bedrooms, with lounge chairs, daybeds, and private plunge pools to dip into. Like the rest of the property, the spa is folded into nature—stroll through tropical gardens to reach the gate, where you'll enter before your treatment. Complimentary yoga, meditation, and Pilates classes are held each morning too, in a pavilion overlooking the ocean. —Madison Flager

Reopened in October 2017 as an Oetker Collection member (formerly a Rosewood resort), Jumby Bay Island is accessible only by boat, with not a car in sight—though there are plenty of bikes available to navigate this 300-acre island off the northern coast of Antigua. With only 40 accommodations in total—rooms and villas— you'll never feel the need to get off the all-inclusive island (although, if curious, there is a complimentary ferry service to the mainland). You’ll be plenty busy on one of the resort’s three tennis courts, in one of the three pools, or on the more than four miles of beach. The cheerful decor throughout the property is the work of Brazilian interior designer Patricia Anastassiadis, of Anastassiadis Arquitetos. —Rosalyn Wikeley

This is paradise in the Caribbean: a tranquil and secluded adults-only all-inclusive retreat with gourmet dining, a dreamy swath of beach with crystal-clear water, warm and friendly staff, and the most serene atmosphere possible. The only “soundtrack” to the property is the crashing waves that can be heard from all of the resort’s 98 rooms, all of which are situated directly on the beach and feature king beds, making this ideal for a romantic getaway. The premium suites offer guests the option to be either on the beach level with direct access to the water, or the upper level with 30-foot-tall vaulted ceilings and a private balcony with glorious ocean views. Galley Bay’s award-winning spa is worth a visit if only because it has two open-air treatment cabanas (one of which accommodates couples) where guests can listen to the sounds of nature while getting a signature massage. —Sara Liss

Hugging the island’s south coast, this small but perfectly formed estate encompasses 19 acres of manicured gardens, all set against a dramatic backdrop of turquoise waters and pink-hued Caribbean sunsets. Each of the suites oozes timeless, old-school charm, featuring colonial accents and period furnishings: think grand four-posters and mahogany furniture. Wake up to languid breakfasts on the beach before working on your tan (don't forget sunscreen!) along the hotel’s palm-fringed sands—and if you’re tempted to explore further afield, you’ll be in the ideal location for sightseeing, with Antigua’s famed Shirley Heights and Nelson’s Dockyard both a stone’s throw away.

A bridge across a sparkling koi pond leads to Carlisle Bay's grand lobby, an open-air space with a colonial design sense and louvred windows that welcome the Caribbean breezes in. There's a real sense of place, and glimpses of the ocean waters and the hotel's private sweep of sand draw your eyes outside. The hotel's 87 ocean-facing suites boast minimalist decor, floor-to-ceiling windows, and fresh flowers. Water sports like wakeboarding, tubing, and waterskiing take place in a neighboring cove, and four unique restaurants mean you never have to leave the property if you don't want to.—Terry Ward

This family-owned resort is nestled within a private bay on the island’s northwestern coast, encompassing a quaint 17 acres of tropical foliage and powder-soft sand beaches. Colonial-style bedrooms have been carefully refreshed with elegant furnishings, and all have their own private terraces or balconies—with a handful of larger villas ideal for family takeovers. The hotel’s four bars and restaurants offer everything from elevated suppers to relaxed dining with your toes in the sand, and days are spent alternating between reef snorkeling, boat rides, and exploring the shoreline’s coves.

Every hotel on this list has been selected independently by our editors and written by a Condé Nast Traveler journalist who knows the destination and has visited that property. When choosing hotels, our editors consider properties across price points that offer an authentic and insider experience of a destination, keeping design, location, service, and sustainability credentials top of mind.

#6281. American Airlines Makes Hotel Vouchers Easier To Get, But Warns Of Fewer Hotel Choices

American Airlines is updating how it provides hotel rooms, food credits, and transportation to passengers stranded by flight disruptions. Getting help without standing in another long line is welcome. But an internal memo also warns that employees may have fewer hotel choices to offer, which leaves me wondering whether a faster voucher will necessarily mean a better night.

View From The Wing highlights a November employee memo outlining changes to American’s Hotel, Meal and Transportation system, known internally as HMT.

American was already promoting automatic disruption vouchers in 2025. The question now is whether the latest changes make that assistance more reliable and easier to use.

I recently wrote about my American Airlines flight from Chicago to Los Angeles that nearly became an overnight stay.

A 7:10 p.m. departure slipped repeatedly until the posted departure time reached 11:55 p.m. The aircraft was there, but we had no pilots. Eventually, pilots arrived from Dallas and received a chorus of cheers from passengers who were thrilled we might actually get home.

During the wait, an Admirals Club agent offered me a hotel room if I wanted to rebook for the next day. The offer came with a caveat:

I appreciated having an option, but I wanted to get to Los Angeles. By that point, an airport hotel would have meant a short night followed by another trip through security and another flight.

But it is a reason why I appreciate this new rollout. Every minute spent waiting for an agent to arrange accommodation is a minute you cannot spend sleeping. If American can deliver a usable hotel offer to your phone promptly, that is a practical improvement.

“Frontline teams may see fewer hotel choices displayed than they are accustomed to seeing.”

Yes, a shorter list of suitable properties could work perfectly well and it is too early to say whether the remaining hotel options will be worse. But I’m not all that optimistic, here.

What happens when the available hotel is far from the airport, has no functioning shuttle at that hour, or cannot accommodate a family in an appropriate room.

We are not talking about putting every stranded passenger in a luxury hotel. But I do expect a clean room and a workable way to get there and back. A voucher is useful only if the accommodation behind it is suitable.

My agent’s Hilton comment was amusing, but it also captured the uncertainty. When you accept an airline-arranged room late at night, you may have little idea what you are getting.

Uber Central allows businesses to request rides for customers who do not have the Uber app. Riders receive trip details and a tracking link by text.

That could be particularly helpful for someone who rarely uses rideshare services or is already overwhelmed by a disrupted journey.

According to the reported instructions, however, hotel shuttles remain the first option, followed by Uber vouchers. Agent-arranged rides are intended for exceptions when those options do not meet the passenger’s needs. Broad availability of the new arrangement has not yet been established.

I hope agents have enough discretion to solve the actual problem. A hotel shuttle listed in a database is no help if it stopped running an hour ago…as a practical aside, before you leave the airport terminal call the hotel to make sure that the shuttle is running.

Under American’s published customer service plan, when a disruption is caused by the airline, assistance available upon request includes:

The plan also promises reimbursement of reasonable hotel costs if American cannot provide an approved hotel voucher (with an almost impossible caveat that such authorization must be obtained in writing). For disruptions beyond its control, such as weather, American generally leaves passengers responsible for their own accommodation and meals.

If you qualify for assistance and no automatic offer arrives, ask an agent. And if you get the food/beverage voucher, realize that the $12 won’t go very far (unless you are in Denver).

American Airlines deserves credit for making disruption assistance easier to deliver. Passengers who have already lost hours to a delay should not have to lose another hour obtaining a hotel voucher.

But fewer hotel choices could limit the usefulness of that improvement. I will judge the system by whether it gets stranded passengers into suitable rooms promptly, with transportation that actually works.

On my recent Chicago flight, I was thankful the pilots arrived and I never needed the hotel. Next time, I may not be so fortunate…(or maybe next time I will fly Delta or United).

#6280. My First “New” Chase Sapphire Reserve Travel Redemption Blew My Mind

There’s… a lot… of coverage surrounding the revamped Chase Sapphire Reserve Card. As per usual these days, the hot takes are plentiful and people are fired up. It’s either the apocalypse or the beginning of something great, depending on which attention seeker you read. As a long time cardholder, I’m really intrigued by the new changes.

The changes really fit my profile and sure, the card will cost more, but I won’t have to introduce any behavior change to get more, unlike some other cards. I’ll do most of my spending on this card. I’m a keeper just from the fee credit and earning multipliers.

Well, if my first Chase Sapphire Reserve redemption is any indicator, this card may single handedly change the redemption game and just about everyone should take note — including airline and hotel transfer partners. It’s already a huge win.

Chase Travel’s ‘The Edit’ is a curated selection of nice hotels, which offer benefits similar to those provided by a travel agent or other luxury credit card booking platform. When booking a ‘The Edit’ property, you can expect breakfast for two, a $100 F&B credit, late check out and an upgrade subject to availability.

Which leads me to the important bit! With the revamped Sapphire Reserve Card, there’s a new “Points Boost” feature, which offers up to two cents per point (25,000 points would cover $500, etc) for some flight or hotel purchases.

This can be amazing value, with flights of $3,000 being grabbed for just 150,000 points, with no taxes and fees and the ability to still earn frequent flyer miles and elite status points, since the airline treats it like a cash ticket.

Previously, the Sapphire Reserve card offered a steady point redemption opportunity directly on Chase Travel at 1.5 cents per point (100,000 points would cover $1500, etc). But with the new version, some travel purchases you want to redeem for will either offer less value than before, the same, or more, with this new ‘Points Boost’ at 2 cents per point. We like more!

I am in New York and wanted to do a little staycation, so I fired up Chase Travel and found one of my more reliable upper mid-scale hotels, The Thompson Central Park was on as part of ‘The Edit’. My two options became a very clear singular, third option.

Typically, I’d consider paying cash or transferring my points from Chase to Hyatt to pay for a stay like this. Hyatt has “fixed” points rates, meaning the points price is largely irrespective of the cash price and only changes by seasonal dates. For this season, it was 25,000 points per night for the Thompson Central Park.

If I were to transfer my points, I’d get a free night (the cash rate was around $500) and have a really solid points redemption at exactly two cents per point. I’m not loyal to any hotel chain really, so I wouldn’t get any breakfast or “elite” benefits, but a free night is a free night.

BUT — Chase Travel had a ‘Points Boost’ option to book the hotel directly on their platform and not transfer points to Hyatt. Chase Travel was offering this property for circa 25,000 points and that would cover the $500 cash rate, but unlike transferring points to Hyatt, because I was redeeming a ‘The Edit’ property on Chase Travel, I’d receive…

Yep, by NOT transferring my points (and dealing with the fractured transfer journey) I was able to get myself basically $200 in additional value added to my stay with the breakfast and $100 property credit, not factoring in the value of late check out or a category room upgrade. In addition, I’ll be able to earn elite nights and Hyatt Points on the stay.

A mere 25,000 Chase Ultimate Rewards Points got me a “free” $500 hotel night, breakfast for two, and $100 to spend at the hotel. That’s a pretty stunning redemption, giving more than two cents per point of value and still allowing me to earn on the stay, unlike when you transfer your points to a loyalty program. I wish I could’ve stayed longer.

For the first time I can remember, transferring points to Hyatt was not the best option here and that’s something to stand up and take notice of.

If Chase can keep up this Points Boost game, it can really send ripples through rewards. For the first time, people can easily receive tremendous value for their points through a credit card portal while still earning elite status and points with the hotel or airline of their choosing.

You can check out the new 100,000 point + 500 travel credit offer for the Sapphire Reserve. It’s 200,000 points for Sapphire Reserve Business Cards.

#6279. The Best Blanket Scarves to Keep You Warm at 30,000 Feet

Anyone who has spent hours on a freezing airplane knows that a warm scarf can make all the difference. A blanket scarf is one of my favorite in-flight essentials: It's easy to throw on before boarding, doubles as an extra layer when cabin temperatures drop, and makes even the simplest airport outfit feel more put together. The best blanket scarves for travel balance comfort, versatility, and style. A large scarf can double as a shawl or blanket on long-haul flights, while lightweight cashmere scarves keep you warm without taking up too much room in your carry-on. Below, I've rounded up the best blanket scarves to travel with this season, from soft, oversized knits to packable, 100% cotton styles.

For those who prefer classic cashmere scarves, Aritzia's blanket scarf checks all the boxes. Made from 100% mid-weight cashmere, the soft jersey knit provides plenty of warmth without feeling too heavy. A narrow silhouette and rolled hem offer it a streamlined look. The cashmere is also verified to The Good Cashmere Standard, which promotes improved animal welfare practices.

The beauty of Eileen Fisher's Triangle scarf lies in how many ways you can wear it. Its triangular shape looks great draped over the shoulders, wrapped around the neck, or loosely tied for a more relaxed look. Made from fine Italian cashmere designed to grow softer over time, this versatile piece is one you'll reach for well beyond a single season.

There may be no brand more synonymous with cashmere than White + Warren, so it’s no surprise that its travel wrap is one of my favorites. I carried a navy version of it all over the country last winter, from a trip to The Green O in Montana down to Primland in Virginia. The light cashmere weave adds warmth without bulk, and its extra-long size means it can drape over my whole body during a plane nap.

Think of Free People's packable scarf as a miniature puffer jacket for your neck. Made from padded nylon, it's a cozy option for winter travel and outdoor adventures, whether you're checking into a cozy cabin or a ski resort. A concealed zip pocket keeps small essentials close, and the included pouch makes it easy to tuck into your carry-on or tote bag.

Long flights, chilly train rides, and overzealous air conditioning are no match for Zestt Organics' Dreamsoft travel scarf. Made from plush, 100% organic cotton, this large scarf measures 28x78" and doubles as a cozy shawl or travel blanket when you need extra coverage. It's also machine washable, making it an especially practical companion for trips near and far.

J.Crew's cashmere wrap, which comes in a range of colors from classic black to camel, is both cozy and sustainable. It's very oversized, keeping you fully covered on the plane, in the car, or even just on the couch. Even better, the company is the first US partner of Aid by Trade Foundation, a nonprofit that promotes sustainable agricultural development around the world.

Gap’s chic scarf combines cozy sherpa with edgy faux leather for an unexpected mix of textures. The rich, on-trend chocolate brown shade makes it especially appealing this season, perfect for city trips and holiday outings. Pair it with a wool coat or leather jacket, et voila.

Until Quince came along, it seemed that affordable cashmere was an oxymoron. But this direct-to-consumer brand has continually surprised me with the high quality of its products at prices that won’t make me cringe. Quince’s ribbed wrap is no exception: It’s a thick, sturdy weave that’s equally perfect around shoulders or as a lap blanket.

Sure, nothing is as soft as cashmere, but when it comes to keeping you toasty, no material beats a wool weave. Alo's wool scarf is very oversized; you can loop it around your neck several times or easily drape it on your shoulders during a chilly flight. Thanks to its extra-long length and thick material, it's a go-to for commerce editor Meaghan Kenny in the winter.

Who says scarves have to be strictly practical? Sofia Cashmere's wrap brings a little sparkle to cold-weather dressing with shimmering metallic fibers, delicate beading, and sequins. The soft, cashmere-blend knit drapes elegantly over the shoulders, adding a stylish finishing touch to fancier looks for holiday parties, evening outings, and winter weddings.

Material: Cashmere, metallic fibers, nylon

Jacquemus' Carro scarf is anything but subtle. Measuring nearly eight-and-a-half feet long, this oversized scarf takes winter accessorizing to the next level. The fuzzy, mohair-alpaca blend adds texture, and there's also an embroidered grosgrain logo. Wrap it around your neck a few times or let the extra-long ends hang loose for maximum impact.

As the name implies, this wrap is a generous piece of fabric that’s 44" wide by 72" long. The material is a sleek mix of 95% Tencel modal and 5% spandex; the stretch is key for allowing it to drape just so. I love that it comes in a handful of seasonal colors, from a deep plum you can even wear to a fancy dinner, to a muted sand that would pair well with anything in your suitcase. Plus, it’s fully machine washable and can go in the dryer without shrinking.

A blanket scarf is a large, oversized wrap that offers more coverage than a traditional scarf. Typically made from cozy materials like wool, cashmere, or cotton, you can wrap it around your neck, drape it over your shoulders, or wear it as a shawl. Some are even large enough to double as a blanket.

Blanket scarves are especially useful for air travel because they can serve as both a stylish accessory and an extra layer when cabin temperatures drop. Look for soft, breathable fabrics like cotton or cashmere that feel comfortable against your skin.

What are the most packable blanket scarves?

The most packable blanket scarves are typically made from lightweight, flexible fabrics that fold down easily without taking up too much suitcase space. Cashmere scarves are a great option because they provide warmth without excessive bulk. For something specifically designed for travel, Free People's Pixie Packable Puffer scarf folds into an included pouch, while Zestt Organics' Dreamsoft travel scarf offers the versatility of a scarf, shawl, and blanket all in one.

#6278. Can you save money with a theme park annual pass? We did the math

Annual passes to major U.S. theme parks like Walt Disney World, Universal Orlando Resort, SeaWorld and Legoland come with a long list of benefits. You can visit as often as you like; you get discounts on extras like parking, merchandise and dining; and your pass often comes with access to special events throughout the year.

Theme park annual passes also come with a hefty price tag that can climb upward of $1,000. Because of this, it can be easy to assume an annual pass is only worth the cost if you live near one of these parks and can visit every week.

As an out-of-state resident who has held an annual pass to Universal Orlando Resort since 2020, I can assure you that assumption is incorrect. But you don't have to take my word for it.

I calculated the break-even point for 10 theme parks across the country to help you decide whether it's an option worth looking into. For consistency, I based these calculations on each park's top-tier pass and the lowest one-day ticket prices, using park-to-park tickets at resorts with multiple parks, since annual passes include park-to-park access.

Because these calculations are based on one-day tickets, you would still need to determine whether you could save money with an annual pass by considering the ticket cost on the date(s) of your visit (most parks have variable pricing), how many trips you take each year and the number of days you visit per trip.

**About 6 once you factor in the cost of free parking and the Express passes

Disney World offers several annual passes, but only one, the Disney Incredi-Pass, is available to out-of-state residents. The Disney Incredi-Pass has no blockout dates and includes complimentary theme park parking.

If you were to visit only on the cheapest days of the year, you would need to visit nine times each year to realize the value of a Disney World annual pass as a non-Florida resident. When you factor in shopping and dining discounts and free parking, you can probably break even after eight visits. But if you were to visit on the more expensive days, you could break even in closer to six days.

Related: Bluey, Buzz and Grogu: Opening dates for new Disney World and Disneyland attractions in 2026

Remember, though, this comparison is based on the one-day ticket price. If you plan to spend eight days at Disney World broken up between one or two visits per year, you could potentially do better to buy a multiday park hopper ticket versus an annual pass. Because Disney uses variable ticket pricing and tickets get less expensive as you add more days, you have to do the math to find out which is best for you.

Don't worry, the math on most other parks isn't quite as involved.

Disneyland's top-tier pass is called the Inspire Key. At $1,899 per year, this pass has blackout dates during the weeks of Christmas and New Year's Eve, and it includes free standard parking and unlimited Disney PhotoPass downloads.

The Inspire Key pass can pay for itself after 11 visits, since the lowest park hopper tickets start at $179.

Related: How Disneyland's newest ride proves that 'progress is impossible without change'

As with Disney World, the number of visits required to break even would decrease if you visited on more expensive days, and you could still save money by purchasing multiday tickets.

Universal Orlando has several annual pass options, but the 2-Park Premier Pass is the easiest to use and has the most benefits. You get park-to-park admission between Universal Studios Florida and Universal Islands of Adventure, complimentary skip-the-line Express passes after 4 p.m., complimentary valet and prime parking, one free ticket to Halloween Horror Nights, early park admission and several valuable discounts.

If you were to visit during the holidays when one-day park-to-park tickets climb as high as $255, you can break even after four days. It's also worth doing the calculations with the included Halloween Horror Nights ticket, which starts at $99. When you factor that in, you can break even after five visits.

Related: Epic Universe tips: 11 ways to spend less time in line and have more fun

A six-day park-to-park ticket that also includes access to Universal Epic Universe is only $550.99 per person, so if you only plan to visit once per year for six days, you would save significantly by purchasing a multiday ticket versus an annual pass.

Universal Studios Hollywood only has one park, making the math here easier to calculate. The park's Platinum Annual Pass has no blockout dates and includes free general parking most of the year, one Halloween Horror Nights ticket and Express skip-the-line access after 3 p.m.

You'd technically have to visit 6.0025 times to break even, but if you include the free parking and after-3 p.m. Express passes, we can safely say you break even after six visits.

Related: Thrills for all ages: 6 best rides at Universal Studios Hollywood

Similar to Universal Orlando, you can break even sooner if you factor in the cost of a Halloween Horror Nights ticket, which starts at $77 per person. When you factor that in, plus those other perks, you can break even after approximately five one-day visits.

This is where things get a little bit fun (in my opinion, anyway). Legoland's Premium Annual Pass includes visits to more than 20 Merlin attractions across the country, including Legoland, Peppa Pig Park, Sea Life Aquarium, Madame Tussauds wax museum and more. A lot of these parks are in theme park hubs like Florida, California and Texas, so you likely aren't too far from one or multiple locations.

In this case, you don't need to plan multiple visits to a single park to see the value in an annual pass. You can visit multiple locations around the country with no blockout dates, free parking and four free "Bring-a-Friend" tickets (one ticket per quarter), which make the math very appealing.

If you assign a $69 value to the "Bring-A-Friend" tickets, four per year would equal $276, just $23 less than the total annual pass cost. So, if you were to visit one of the 20+ parks nationwide four times per year (once per quarter) and bring a friend or family member with you, you'd save money with an annual pass before even factoring in free parking and other discounts.

This is another instance where you can access multiple parks with a single annual pass. SeaWorld Orlando's Platinum Pass includes unlimited admission to 11 parks across the country with no blockout dates. These include all SeaWorld and Busch Gardens parks, as well as their affiliated water parks. You also get eight free guest tickets, free photos and free preferred parking.

A few notes here. You can't use all eight free guest tickets at the same time and they are limited to select parks. SeaWorld allows you to use a certain number of tickets during different calendar windows throughout the year. But if you were to visit these parks eight times per year and bring a friend, you would save more than $600 by purchasing an annual pass.

It's also worth noting that SeaWorld San Diego's Platinum Pass is only $201 on sale, and its lowest one-day ticket costs $64.99, so you'd break even after just four visits. While it provides the passholder access to the same 11 parks, its guest passes can only be used at the California parks.

Opened in July 2026, Universal Kids Resort is the newest park on this list. The park recently started selling annual passes, with the Gold Annual Pass being its top-tier offering. The Gold pass has no blockout dates and includes regular self-parking.

Assuming you visit on five separate days and only visit on the least expensive days, you would break even after five visits. But because the Gold Pass also includes free parking and other discounts, you could potentially break even in four one-day visits. Because the park also sells discounted multiday tickets, the above math only makes sense if you were to visit on five nonconsecutive days.

You don't need to live in Florida or California to have access to award-winning theme parks. Holiday World in Santa Claus, Indiana, consistently wins awards for its cleanliness, water park and thrilling coasters. Holiday World's Platinum Pass has no blockout dates, early entry for select attractions and discounted "Bring-a-Friend" tickets.

Holiday World already offers free parking, sunscreen and soft drinks, so you won't get additional discounts there. You would break even after four one-day visits, assuming you purchase the lowest-cost tickets.

Dollywood's top-of-the-line pass is a Diamond Season Pass (a very fitting name for our bright and shining queen Dolly Parton, if you ask me). With it, you get unlimited visits, complimentary parking, Time Saver skip-the-line access for the first hour of each day, a 20% discount on shopping and dining, and four free "Bring-a-Friend" tickets.

Dollywood handles its "Bring-a-Friend" tickets differently. You can use them one at a time or all four at once. If you brought four friends with you during your first visit after buying your annual pass, you would have more than covered the cost of your pass. In fact, you could save about $110 by purchasing an annual pass instead of five one-day tickets (you and four friends). Any future visits that year are just a bonus. Just one of the million reasons to love Dollywood.

Silver Dollar City and Dollywood are owned by the same parent company (Herschend Family Entertainment), but their annual passes work quite differently. Silver Dollar City's Diamond Pass includes unlimited visits to the park and White Water water park, eight free "Bring A Friend" tickets (to be used during specific redemption windows at Silver Dollar City or White Water), a bonus "Bring-a-Friend" ticket you can use on any day and $29.99 tickets for friends and family.

Even though you can't use all of your "Bring-a-Friend" tickets at one time, you only need to visit with a guest twice to break even with an annual pass before even digging into the savings you would find from in-park discounts.

In addition to the advertised benefits, there is a level of convenience that comes with being a passholder. You can pop in for a few hours without feeling like you wasted money on a full-day ticket, and you feel like a more valuable guest when you visit. I often get things like priority parade seating, fun freebies and passholder-only discounts of up to 70% off merchandise.

No amount of math matters unless you know you will actually use and enjoy the benefits of being a passholder. Use these calculations as a jumping-off point to decide if you are ready to be a passholder.

#6277. Southwest Airlines Offers “Free” Same-Day Flight Changes, But There’s A Seat-Fee Trap

Southwest Airlines offers eligible passengers free same-day flight changes, but there is a catch if you paid separately for your seat. Asking an airport agent to make the change can leave that seat purchase nonrefundable, while making the change through the app, website, or telephone receives different treatment. Apparently, how you change your flight now matters almost as much as which flight you choose.

View From The Wing highlights a peculiar provision in Southwest’s seat refund and exchange policy.

For passengers who separately purchased a seat on their original flight, Southwest explicitly states:

“Same-day change requested at the airport: Seat purchased on original flight is non-refundable.”

But complete that same-day change through Southwest.com, the Southwest app, or by telephone, and the rules provide a way to apply the original seat payment toward a replacement or receive a refund when buying a more expensive seat.

You could be standing at the gate with your phone in hand, looking at an earlier departure. Whether you tap the screen or ask the employee in front of you for help could affect what happens to money you already spent.

The policy concerns seats purchased separately from the airfare. Here is how Southwest describes the treatment when you voluntarily switch flights:

For a hypothetical example, suppose you paid $40 for a seat and make a confirmed same-day change through the app. If the replacement seat costs $30, Southwest applies the original payment but does not return the $10 difference.

If the replacement costs $50, you pay $50 upfront and generally receive a separate $40 refund. You should therefore check that the refund actually arrives rather than assuming the system simply charged you the difference.

Under Southwest’s same-day change policy, the confirmed-change benefit is available with Choice, Choice Preferred, and Choice Extra fares, along with Getaways by Southwest vacation bookings.

You need an available seat on a flight between the same origin and destination airports on the same travel date. The change must occur at least 10 minutes before your original scheduled departure.

Basic passengers must upgrade to an eligible fare first (and A-List or A-List Preferred status alone does not make a Basic ticket eligible for a free confirmed same-day change)

So when it comes to standby, there are two separate things to check: whether you can switch flights without an additional airfare charge, and what happens to the seat you purchased.

Do not confuse a confirmed change with same-day standby.

A confirmed change secures your place on the replacement flight immediately. Standby means waiting for space to become available, often much closer to boarding or even after boarding commences if you are waiting for no-shows. Southwest’s seat policy says the original seat purchase becomes nonrefundable when standby clears, regardless of how you joined the list.

Using the app therefore does not solve the seat-payment issue for standby. The eligibility rules differ too. A-List and A-List Preferred members can qualify for standby on Basic fares, even though those fares do not qualify for free confirmed same-day changes.

Of course, switching flights does not guarantee the same seat. Someone who bought extra legroom on one departure cannot reasonably expect an identical seat to materialize on a replacement flight. But why should the channel used to request the change determine the treatment of the original payment?

If Southwest can apply or refund that purchase when I use its app, why should asking an airport employee produce a less favorable rule? There may be a systems explanation, but that does little for a passenger who reasonably assumes an agent can provide the same options available online. On the other hand, I would bet that an agent who assigns you a superior seat in these sorts of situations is not going to charge for it…any frequent Southwest travelers want to weigh in?

This also puts employees in an awkward position. A passenger asks for help, receives it, then discovers that handling the transaction another way could have preserved the value of a seat purchase. For an airline that built so much goodwill around simplicity, this seems like an unnecessarily complicated way to handle a relatively ordinary request.

If you paid separately for a Southwest seat and want to make a confirmed same-day flight change, check the app or website before asking an airport agent to process it. Telephone changes also receive the more favorable treatment outlined in the policy.

Compare the replacement seat cost and keep track of any refund due. If you are using standby, remember that the app does not preserve the refundability of your original seat purchase once you clear.

A free flight change can still have consequences for the extras you purchased. Southwest passengers now have another reason to read the fine print before accepting what sounds like a straightforward benefit.

I often tell people that the best unkept secret with Avios is, in fact, the Avios app. Separate to the British Airways app, the Avios app allows users to set flight alerts and goals, but also gives a heads up about opportunities before they appear anywhere else.

This isn’t the first time Avios has launched a flight only bookable with points, but it is the first time they’ve done one to CAPE TOWN, during peak winter break time.

As noted, these flights are now bookable and if history repeats itself, they won’t be available for long. This plane only has 8 seats in first, so get in quick! #6275. KLM Plans 1,000 More Job Cuts

KLM expects to eliminate approximately 1,000 positions through productivity improvements as part of a restructuring announced Thursday.

The Dutch carrier said it would seek to limit the impact through natural attrition, voluntary arrangements and transfers. Other changes include moving about 800 ground services positions to outside providers and transferring 2,000 positions to Air France-KLM, including 1,500 at customer contact center Cygnific.

“But KLM’s future is not guaranteed,” CEO Marjan Rintel said in a statement, citing global instability, high fuel prices, and pressure on the industry.

KLM is targeting a structural productivity increase of at least 8% by 2028, alongside restrained wage growth. It said an additional €1 billion in annual earnings improvement is needed to fund investments.

The changes also affect its European fleet. KLM will replace planned Airbus A320s with Embraer E195-E2s, giving regional subsidiary Cityhopper a larger role. The A321neo will remain, while Boeing 737s and Embraer E190s will be phased out.

The announcement came as KLM reported a third-quarter operating profit of €458 million, up from €352 million a year earlier. For the first nine months of 2026, operating profit reached €526 million on revenue of €10.9 billion.

Despite the improvement, KLM said profitability remains insufficient to support its investment needs. Higher fuel costs and Middle East flight cancellations weighed on its passenger business, while Transavia faced competition and operational challenges.

“We need to increase it to more than 8% to secure a financially healthy future for KLM,” Chief Financial Officer Bas Brouns said of the airline’s profit margin.

#6274. 10 Spacious Villas in Morocco Fit for a Relaxing Group Getaway

The bustling capital city has perennial charm, but beyond its walls, there’s so much more to Morocco worth exploring. Whether you’re gearing up for a hiking trip to the Atlas mountains, looking to immerse yourself in the sights and sounds of the buzzy souks or headed out to the coast, there’s a fantastic nearby address to know. Most of our favorite Morocco villas pair idyllic views with in-house chefs, housekeepers, and even security staff for a hotel-worthy break in your own space. Below are 10 of the best villas in Morocco to rent for your next trip.

We've vetted these listings based on Superhost or Guest Favorite status, ratings, amenities, location, previous guest reviews, and decor.

Bed & bath: 5 bedrooms, 5 bathroomsTop amenities: Heated pool, home cinema, sauna and steam room

This is the kind of holiday home that keeps everyone happy, making it perfect for a large family with different ideas of what a great holiday looks like. The interiors are modern, but Moroccan charm is preserved in the details. The five spacious bedrooms all feature en suite bathrooms and are spread across both floors. The large living area, with its circular arrangement of comfortable sofas, and the home cinema invite guests to relax and enjoy each other's company during their stay. A fitness center and a traditional hammam add a wellness touch to the home. There is a golf course right next door, should you fancy a round of golf.

Bed & bath: 8 bedrooms, 7 bathroomsTop amenities: Pool, hammam, pickleball court, pétanque, barbecue

Located just north of Marrakech, this villa gives groups a soft, quiet place to land after a busy day in the city—and plenty of activities to keep everyone busy on days spent on-site. Beyond the resort-style heated swimming pool lined with lounge chairs, the pétanque and pickleball courts encourage some healthy competition. Afterwards, spend a bit of relaxation time in the hammam or massage room, or kick back in the garden. Of note, two of the eight bedrooms are located in an annex of the villa and share a bathroom.

Bed & bath: 6 bedrooms, 6 bathroomsTop amenities: Heated pool, outdoor dining space

To reach this villa, you have to drive 30 minutes from Marrakech into the stunning Ourika Valley. On arrival, you’ll immediately notice the snow-capped peaks of the Atlas Mountains rising around the property. The 8,000-square-meter garden dotted with olive trees and cacti is the perfect setting for days spent lying by the large pool, playing pétanque, or cooking up a storm with produce from the organic kitchen garden. Inside, the house is bathed in sunlight and particularly stunning at dawn. There are six bedrooms, all featuring en suite bathrooms for ultimate comfort. Five of the bedrooms are in the main house—as well as the kitchen and the spacious living room featuring a dining space with a fireplace—while the final bedroom is in the annex, alongside the playroom and wellness area with a hammam.

Bed & bath: 6 bedrooms, 6 bathsTop amenities: Terrace, pool, hot tub, gym

Bed & bath: 6 bedrooms, 7 bathsTop amenities: Pool, terraces, Atlas Mountains views

Palais Les Orchidées is a palace-like six-suite villa just outside the center of Marrakech, combining grand architecture with pared-back interiors and views towards the Atlas Mountains. The property is surrounded by leafy gardens, with a large swimming pool and several terraces providing plenty of space to relax outdoors. Inside, all six suites have king-size beds and en suite bathrooms with bathtubs and showers, making this a particularly comfortable option for a large group or several couples traveling together. Despite its peaceful setting, you won’t be too far from the action: the villa is around 15 minutes by car from some of Marrakech’s best-known sights, including the Koutoubia, Bahia Palace, and Jardin Majorelle, and around 20 minutes from Marrakech Menara Airport. Breakfast can also be served at the villa for an additional charge.

Bed & bath: 5 bedrooms, 5 bathsTop amenities: Rooftop terrace, private pool, breakfast chef

This classic Marrakech riad is a bohemian dream with vibrant, patterned tiles, a mishmash of colorful, soft furnishings, and a beautiful outdoor courtyard—bringing good vibes only. You’ll be well taken care of here; daily housekeeping, a breakfast chef, and a night guard will ensure everything goes swimmingly. Take an alfresco lunch before a dip in the plunge pool, then settle on the daybed for a leisurely afternoon with a view—there’s a panoramic vista of both the buzzing medina and the Atlas mountain range. Take note: You’ll have to climb some steps to reach this villa, and there’s no parking outside, so if you’re taking a car, you’ll need to leave it a short distance away. However, there are a slew of excellent restaurants and hammams within walking distance and good public transport links right outside.

Bed & bath: 9 bedrooms, 9 bathsTop amenities: Outdoor kitchen, sauna/steam room, gym

Like most experiences in Morocco, stepping into this palatial villa’s vast grounds is a sensory feast from the get-go. Plaster pink walls, an eclectic mix of bright furniture, ornate artwork, patterned rugs, and glittering chandeliers are wrapped around the central turquoise jewel of the outdoor pool. It has nine huge bedrooms, at least one of which has a statement roll-top tub in the corner, plus nine bathrooms—so no waiting in line for the shower here. It’s a great choice for bachelor or bachelorette parties and big group getaways, with multiple comfy gathering spaces for catch-ups with a view. First, head to the meeting room to grab a drink from the bar, but take them to the rooftop terrace to maximize the experience—the views at sunset are fantastic. Extra bookable spa and hammam treatments make a stay in this Moroccan palace all the sweeter.

Bed & bath: 8 bedrooms, 8 bathsTop amenities: Private pool, courtyard, outdoor shower, record player

This isn’t a riad, but a former fondouk—a 19th-century inn that used to accommodate travelers before they set sail on trading voyages. Now, however, it has been transformed into a chic villa for 15, set around four distinct courtyard spaces decorated with fragrant lemon trees and mature prickly cacti. Locally sourced clay walls bring traditional flair that keeps you cool on hot Moroccan nights, and there’s a pool to jump into for welcome midday dips. Active types, take note. This villa sits in the ancient walled city of Taraudant, which offers easy access to both the High Access and Anti-Atlas hiking routes. It's the perfect place to wind down after a long day of mountain treks.

Bed & bath: 4 bedrooms, 4 bathsTop amenities: Terrace, courtyard, fireplace, private cook

Bed & bath: 2 bedrooms, 3 bathsTop amenities: Private chefs, private heated pool, terrace

With a hilltop location looking down onto sparkling sea views, even by Moroccan standards, the views here are unbeatable. A clever design means the home provides ample opportunity to totally immerse yourself in the landscape. Run a bath in the outdoor tub right on the beachfront, and awake to sunrise light streaming through floor-to-ceiling windows framing gentle ocean waves. Mealtimes are sorted thanks to the in-house private chefs who’ll cook up anything you please to be enjoyed alfresco with a glass of wine on the terrace next to the private heated pool. There’s a slew of activities on offer in Essaouira—tell the hosts what you’d like to do and they’ll make it happen.

That’s changing with the opining tomorrow of the E Concourse expansion and a brand new United Club that is even more beautiful to me than the new Houston lounge.

Even better, Chase Offers can often be combined with your card’s usual earning rates and shopping portals, helping you get more value from everyday spending.

Here’s how the program works and how to maximize it.

Chase Offers is a program available on eligible Chase debit and credit cards that gives cardholders access to targeted deals, similar to Amex Offers. These offers typically provide cash back or a percentage back as a statement credit when you make a qualifying purchase.

Like similar programs from other issuers, offers are personalized. That means the deals you see may differ from what someone else receives. You may also see different offers across your own Chase cards.

Most Chase-issued consumer and business credit and debit cards are eligible for Chase Offers if the primary cardholder has a U.S. address listed as their primary residence or place of business.

To see if Chase Offers is available for your card, check your Chase mobile app or log in at Chase's website.

For Chase credit cards, primary cardholders and authorized officers can view and add offers. Authorized users and employees can't add offers themselves, but they can redeem offers that have already been added to the account.

Some of the most popular eligible cards include:

Chase Offers are also available on many cobranded Chase credit cards, such as the (see rates and fees) and select United Airlines and Marriott Bonvoy cards.

Each card may offer different deals, so it's worth checking all your accounts if you hold more than one Chase card.

You can find available offers on the Chase website and on the Chase app. To view your available offers on the website, log in to your account and find "Chase Offers" on the right-hand panel.

Alternatively, you can click on "Benefits & travel" on the top panel and select "Chase Offers", as shown below. Note that the offers shown below may not be available to you.

To view your Chase Offers on the Chase mobile app, log in to your account and then scroll down toward the middle of the main account dashboard. You should see a section titled “Chase Offers” showing some of your current offers.

Either the website or app option will bring you to the offers currently available for you to browse.

Offerings change daily and typically feature various types of goods and services. You may see deals for:

Offers typically range from about 5% to 30% back or provide a fixed statement credit after meeting a spending requirement. For example, you might receive a $20 statement credit after spending $100 with a specific merchant.

Chase Offers can be an easy way to save on purchases you’re already making, which is something TPG staffers have seen firsthand across a range of everyday spending.

TPG travel writer Rachel Craft, for example, recently used an offer on her for 15% back at home improvement stores. She bundled supplies for a few projects she already had planned into a single purchase and received $33 back. Meanwhile, TPG principal spokesperson Clint Henderson earned an $85 statement credit on a DISH Network purchase using his World of Hyatt card.

TPG editor-in-chief Nick Ewen has also had success with Chase Offers. He recently earned $15.81 back on Trans-Siberian Orchestra tickets purchased through SeatGeek with his Chase Freedom Flex. Since the purchase also fell within one of the card's Q3 rotating quarterly bonus categories, he earned 5% cash back on top of his Chase Offer savings (on up to $1,500 in combined purchases each quarter, activation required).

And in an even bigger example of how these savings can add up, Nick earned a $125 statement credit through a Chase Offer on an IHG hotel stay booked through The Edit by Chase Travel℠, using his . By combining that offer with the card's The Edit and select hotels credits, he saved a total of $625 on the stay.

While individual savings may vary, these examples highlight how these targeted offers can add up, especially on purchases you already planned to make.

While you don’t have to enroll your card to start using the Chase Offers program, you do have to add each individual offer to your credit card. Adding them is easy — all you have to do is navigate to Chase Offers either online or through the Chase Mobile app and click “Add to card” on any available offer that interests you.

Alternatively, if you have a subscription to a service like MaxRewards Gold, your offers should be automatically activated for all linked cards.

Then, use your card at the specific merchant, and you should see a statement credit applied to your account within 30 days after your qualifying transaction posts, unless the offer terms state otherwise.

Once you arrive on the Chase Offers landing page, adding an offer to your account is very simple.

If you have multiple eligible Chase cards, you’ll see a “Choose your account” drop-down near the top of the screen. Note that if you have multiple sign-ins with Chase, such as one for your personal cards and one for business credit cards, you will only see cards associated with the account for which you’re currently signed in.

Again, note that the offers you see here may not be available for you.

Click on any offer to add it to your card. Then, use your card at the specific merchant and wait for your statement credit to post.

Once you find an offer you would like to use in the app, the process is similar to the website process.

You can click on “See all available deals” to see the rest of your offers. You’ll see a “Choose your account” drop-down near the top of the screen if you have multiple eligible Chase cards.

Click on any offers to add them to your card, use your card at the participating merchant and wait for your statement credit to post.

When you add an offer for a specific card, you must use that same card to redeem the offer. For example, if you add a Chase Offer to your , you must use that card to redeem that offer successfully.

Be sure to read the terms and conditions for each offer carefully. You only have a certain amount of time to use each offer, and many come with maximum earning limits. As long as you make your purchase by the expiration date, you should receive the credit even if the transaction posts after the expiration date.

Chase Offers are rewarded as a statement credit, even if you have a card that earns Ultimate Rewards points on regular spending.

One of the common threads among all Chase Offers is this condition: Payment must be made directly with the merchant. While you can still use services like mobile wallets and PayPal with Chase Offers, you can’t use third-party providers to make purchases.

Finally, Chase Offers are only available on eligible U.S.-issued Chase credit cards tied to U.S.-based accounts. However, some offers may still be valid at international merchants, particularly global brands like hotel chains, as long as the transaction is processed by the eligible merchant and charged to your enrolled card.

Since new offers are constantly added, it’s a good idea to go through your Chase Offers at least biweekly to review and add new offers. It doesn’t cost anything to add an offer and then not use it, so you can be pretty lenient with which offers you add.

If there’s even a tiny possibility that you’ll use an offer, you might as well add it to your card. If you use it, great; if not, it’s not a problem.

Chase Offers become significantly more valuable when you stack them with other rewards opportunities. This means combining an offer with a shopping portal and a credit card bonus category to earn multiple layers of rewards on the same purchase.

For example, imagine you’re booking a $200 stay at a Hyatt property. You could:

In this scenario, you’d earn 1,000 points through the portal, $10 cash back from your Freedom Flex and a $20 statement credit from the Chase Offer.

Instead of earning rewards from just one source, you’ve effectively tripled up on the same purchase.

Chase Offers are best used for purchases you were already planning to make. Like any coupon or sale, saving 10% on something you didn’t need isn’t actually saving money. But when used strategically, especially in combination with shopping portals and bonus categories, they can meaningfully boost your overall return.

*Earn 5% cash back in rotating categories for the first $1,500 in combined purchases each quarter; activation required.

Related: How I earned over 3,800 points and miles buying $180 worth of sports tickets with my Freedom Flex

Chase Offers is one of the easiest ways to save money on purchases you already plan to make. While the discounts may not always be large, they require minimal effort and can add up quickly.

By checking your offers regularly and combining them with bonus categories and shopping portals, you can turn everyday spending into meaningful savings over time.
